issues.title: L2-norm definition uses the wrong integrand variable

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The asymptotic character of the characteristic layer $w_T$ is related to the solution $z$ of the singularly perturbed parabolic problem

issues.failure_explanation: The footnote claims that the squared L2 norm of u is the integral of z squared. The old paper has just used z for the solution of a separate singularly perturbed parabolic problem, whereas the energy norm and the left-hand side concern u. Consequently the displayed right-hand side does not define the norm of its stated argument; the supported standard definition is the integral of u squared.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed norm definition is wrong as written, but the later error analysis uses the global pointwise norm, so no formal result depends on this variable error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the integrand z² by u², so the definition reads ||u||²_{L²} := ∫_Ω u² dΩ. No dependent argument or result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The norm named on the left and the adjacent energy-norm formula uniquely force u², while z denotes the unrelated parabolic solution discussed immediately beforehand. No reasoning relies on the erroneous integrand, so this is a uniquely correctable transcription error.

issues.title: Characteristic-layer lemma overstates the uniform N-rate
issues.failure_explanation: Under Assumption (assume), the lemma claims for every mesh point a bound with N-part C(N^{-1} ln N)^2. In the upper characteristic strip, however, its concluding comparison function contains CN^{-1}B_3. The definition at (barrier) gives B_3=1 for x_i>1-τ_x, so this is an O(N^{-1}) contribution; for example with M=N, it cannot be absorbed uniformly into O(N^{-2} ln^2 N). The general truncation bound also contains the mixed characteristic-layer term h_i min(1,h_i/ε) ε|w_{yyx}|, while the supplied characteristic derivative bounds provide no east-boundary decay that would reduce this generically to second order. Thus the old argument supports only the weaker first-order rate in the characteristic strips.
issues.overall_effect: The characteristic-layer component estimates for both the north and south strips are not established at the claimed N-rate, and consequently the old full-domain bounds in main-result are not established. The near-second-order N-rate remains supportable only outside those strips.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the characteristic-layer lemma by regional estimates: retain C[(N^{-1} ln N)²+(M^{-1} ln M)²] for W_N−w_N when y_j ≤ 1−τ_y and for W_S−w_S when y_j ≥ τ_y, but use C[N^{-1}+(M^{-1} ln M)²] in the respective north and south characteristic strips. Propagate the same repair to main-result: retain the old N-rate on [0,1]×[τ_y,1−τ_y], but use C N^{-1} on the full square, with the theorem's applicable general or sharper M-term unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old comparison function contains C N^{-1}B_3, with B_3=1 in the east fine region, and the stated derivative bounds provide no east-boundary decay for the mixed characteristic-layer truncation term. Thus the source-supported repair is first order in the natural characteristic strips. Although the statement-level repair is contained, it lowers the dependent full-domain maximum-norm guarantee by an algebraic order and surrenders its central near-second-order global rate. Recovering the old guarantee would require unsupported new proof or method architecture, while imposing assumptions that suppress the order-one characteristic layers would exclude the regime central to the result. Every established complete route therefore entails major mathematical loss or global reconstruction.
